# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### I/O latency ~504 ms write / ~255 ms read on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** From 16:48 UTC avg write latency rose from ~0.95 ms to ~504 ms and avg read latency from ~0.6 ms to ~255 ms. VolumeQueueLength went from ~0.77 to ~16. Total IOPS fell from ~1,000/s to ~42/s and VolumeIdleTime fell to ~0. The IOPS/Throughput exceeded and StalledIO checks returned no datapoints. The example-d-gp3-queue-length alarm fired at 16:51:48 UTC.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T16:47:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 injecting 500 ms I/O latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 (template EXT1234567890abcdef_4, 'example scenario d: 500 ms EBS I/O latency') was started by example-session at 16:47:04 UTC. Its aws:ebs:volume-io-latency action began at 16:47:16 UTC and adds 500 ms to 100% of writes and 50% of reads on vol-0123456789abcdef0. It runs for PT60M (until ~17:47 UTC) with no stop condition. The application keeps 16 I/Os in flight and each one now waits ~500 ms. As a result the queue sits at ~16, total IOPS fell from ~1,000/s to ~42/s, and the queue-length alarm (threshold 4) fired at 16:51:48 UTC.
**Cascades to:** symptom-write-latency

#### Supporting Observations
- **FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 started by example-session at 16:47:04 UTC:** StartExperiment was called by example-session at 16:47:04 UTC; an earlier run was started at 16:15:35 UTC. Template EXT1234567890abcdef_4 ('example scenario d: 500 ms EBS I/O latency', Name=example-d-latency) was last updated at 16:47:01 UTC and has no stop conditions. Role: example-fis. Target: vol-0123456789abcdef0. The aws:ebs:volume-io-latency action started at 16:47:16 UTC for PT60M (until ~17:47 UTC). It adds 500 ms to 100% of writes and to 50% of reads. Earlier runs of this template: 16:15 and 08:35 (stopped by user), 07:40 (completed).
- **Read latency ~255 ms, matching 50% of reads delayed by 500 ms:** Avg read latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0 went from ~0.59 ms to ~250-262 ms starting 16:48 UTC. Read bytes fell from ~491 MB/min to ~21 MB/min. This matches the FIS action, which delays 50% of reads by 500 ms.
- **d-gp3 queue-length alarm fired at 16:51:48 UTC:** Alarm example-d-gp3-queue-length (VolumeQueueLength > 4, 3x60s) moved from OK to ALARM at 2026-11-23 16:51:48 UTC, about 4.5 minutes after the FIS latency action started. Other eval alarms in ALARM: a-io2 queue length (vol-1234567890abcdef0_4) and b-gp3 read bytes (vol-1234567890abcdef0_18), since ~16:23 UTC.
- **No other control-plane changes on the volume:** CloudTrail for 16:30-16:53 UTC shows no events on vol-0123456789abcdef0. The FIS events in that window are read-only ListExperiments/GetExperimentTemplate calls.

#### Gaps

**Description:** Hypothesis: the latency comes from hitting the provisioned gp3 IOPS/throughput or the instance's EBS limits.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Stop FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 (with owner approval) instead of adding IOPS

## Reasoning
The 500 ms latency is injected by the FIS experiment, capping the volume at ~42 IOPS regardless of provisioning. Before the experiment the volume used ~1,000 of 3,000 IOPS and ~16 of 125 MiB/s. Ending the experiment removes the latency; if nobody acts it ends by itself at ~17:47:16Z. None of these steps have been executed.
